features.limits: The format must be a string literal. Each % consumes one integer, float, bool, string, enum, record, or fixed-array argument; an enum prints as its member name and a record as {x = 1, y = 2}, with strings quoted, fixed arrays up to 16 elements, and Vecs and slices by count; %% prints one percent. Arguments are evaluated left to right before output, and floats use the shortest decimal that round-trips to the same value.
features.rejection: print requires a string literal format.

features.limits: New allocates a zeroed value and free ignores null. Types holding owned Vec storage are rejected. Native callers must release allocations once and preserve pointer lifetimes; Python and the portable VM reject direct reads after free and double frees.
features.rejection: Heap allocation cannot bypass owned Vec cleanup.

features.limits: Locals, parameters, and Vec fields in records/fixed arrays are dropped on scope exit. Moves invalidate their source. Globals are shared storage; indexed and pointer-backed field moves still have restrictions.
features.accepted_example:
#import "vec"
#program_export
Answer :: () -> s32 {
    values: Vec(s32)
    VecPush(values, 42)
    return values[0]
}
features.rejected_example:
#import "vec"
Answer :: () -> s32 {
    values: Vec(s32)
    VecPush(values, 42)
    moved := values
    return values[0]
}
features.rejection: Owned values cannot be read after moving.
